correctness.rationale: Exact domain: every integer dimension at least one, vertex set even subsets, and unrestricted pure-adjacency first-order sentences of rank at most three. The all-dimensional table of two-point extension signatures follows directly from |Z|=2 for neighbors of the empty set and from |D triangle Z|=|D|+|Z|-2|D intersect Z|. Equality cases and all small boundary dimensions are explicit. Four stable pair profiles give a three-round Duplicator strategy. Six depth-at-most-three sentences yield strictly increasing thresholds two through seven, proving pairwise distinction and the sharp family-relative 64-vertex bound. A standalone exact full-graph Hintikka recurrence was run for dimensions one to nine, an independent orbit recurrence through dimension thirteen, and six separating predicates all passed. Finite runs are checks, not infinite proofs.

evidence: The halved cube is the even-parity component of the distance-two graph of a binary hypercube (Krotov 2008, introduction).
It is also isomorphic to the square of a cube one dimension lower, under the usual graph-square convention (halved-cube graph reference).
Searches returned papers on parity reduction of hypercube Rips complexes and multinary Hamming Čech complexes; neither addresses a logical equivalence theorem.

A theorem for ordinary distance-one cube graphs cannot transfer quantifier-rank bounds through graph squaring merely by renaming: interpreting square adjacency requires an existential formula and changes quantifier rank. The nearby Rips/Čech results concern different invariants, and the inspected halved-cube sources do not classify rank-three sentences.

originality.rationale: The cited full-text papers cover the same halved-cube objects but address equitable colorings, clique VC-dimension/edge density, and Terwilliger representations; none of their examined statements implies an ordinary quantifier-rank-three classification. Earlier published work on distance-one Hamming graphs, binary hypercubes, and strongly regular graph extension flags was compared at the claim level: it neither states nor entails the four extension profiles for every halved cube dimension, especially dimensions six and seven. The exact seven-class logical invariant and sharp minimum representative were not located in actual index, primary-literature, or recoverable prior-claim checks. Absence from these sources is evidence, not a guarantee of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible older work could formulate the same finite-rank classification.
General purpose distance-regular graph logical-type results not returned by indexed searches could yield the claim as an unstated specialization; no global uniqueness is asserted.

value.rationale: The natural family of halved cubes is classical in distance-regular graph theory and coding theory. The exact ordinary bounded-rank logical quotient is a complete natural invariant, not a chosen isolated small example: exactly seven classes, a sharp 64-vertex minimal testing bound, and a structural explanation of why a special antipodal extension profile vanishes at dimension seven. It contrasts with the strictly increasing valency and counting-logic observability. The statement is not implied by known spectral, perfect-coloring, or density tables inspected here.
